returned_title: GLES Cross-Section 2021 – German Federal Election Study
justification: A dedicated survey dataset examining German voters before and after the 2021 federal election. Contains individual-level information on electoral choices, party identification, political attitudes, ideological self-placement, political interest, and evaluations of candidates and parties. Provides a valuable empirical baseline for studying political changes during the 2020s, including the transition from Angela Merkel's chancellorship, coalition preferences, and the development of political polarization.

returned_title: GLES Candidate Studies – German Federal Elections 2021 and 2025
justification: Datasets focusing on political candidates and party organisations participating in German federal elections. They provide information relevant to candidate characteristics, political recruitment, ideological positions, political careers, and party affiliations. The GLES collection includes candidate-related studies and nomination studies for the 2021 and 2025 federal elections. Particularly useful for researching political representation, party organisation, candidate selection, and ideological differences among political elites.

returned_title: GLES Nomination Study 2025 – Political Candidate Selection in Germany
justification: A specialised dataset examining candidate nominations for Germany's 2025 federal election, identified by GESIS study number ZA10104. Relevant for investigating internal party organisation, candidate recruitment, political representation, and the processes through which political parties select electoral candidates. Particularly suitable for research on political organisations, party structures, and democratic representation in Germany during the 2020s.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2023 – Full Version
justification: A German population survey dataset providing information on social and political attitudes in 2023. Relevant for analysing political values, social divisions, democratic orientations, institutional confidence, and relationships between demographic characteristics and political preferences. Its detailed demographic information supports research on ideological differences across age groups, educational backgrounds, social classes, and regions of Germany.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2021
justification: A dataset covering social attitudes and values among the German population in 2021. Provides evidence relevant to political ideology, democratic values, institutional trust, social inequality, immigration attitudes, and political engagement. Useful for analysing the social foundations of political behaviour at the beginning of the 2020s and comparing political orientations across population groups.

returned_title: German Federal Election 2025 – Official Constituency and National Results
justification: Official electoral statistics documenting the outcomes of the 2025 Bundestag election at national, state, and constituency levels. Provides authoritative information about party performance, voting patterns, voter turnout, and electoral representation. Relevant for analysing the distribution of political support, regional differences in ideology, and changes in Germany's party system. Particularly useful when combined with survey datasets such as GLES or ALLBUS.

returned_title: Attitudes to College and Politics 1969 (Einstellungen zu Hochschule und Politik 1969)
justification: Highly relevant to all three requested topics. This 1969 survey examines students enrolled at the University of Cologne during the 1967/68 winter semester. It covers higher education conditions, university governance, student political participation, student protests, political organizations, attitudes toward parliamentary democracy, and political party preferences. It also explores attitudes toward government policies, university autonomy, student representation, and the West German political system. Particularly valuable for studying the relationship between higher education and political activism during the German student movement of the late 1960s.

returned_title: Issue Dimensions and Voting Decision (April 1969)
justification: A West German political attitudes survey conducted between April and May 1969. It investigates voting intentions, political party preferences, evaluations of government performance, and attitudes toward major political controversies. Particularly relevant are questions concerning education policy, social policy, political radicalism, recognition of East Germany, and the perceived competence of political parties. The dataset supports research on political behavior, government institutions, and the importance of educational issues in electoral politics.

returned_title: German Pre- and Post-Election Study, 1969
justification: A comprehensive survey conducted before and after the 1969 West German federal election. It includes information about political participation, voter attitudes, party identification, political knowledge, government evaluations, and perceptions of political leaders. The study also examines public attitudes toward domestic policy issues and the ability of political parties to address national problems. Respondent characteristics permit investigation of relationships between educational background and political behavior. Particularly useful for examining democratic participation and electoral politics in West Germany at the end of the 1960s.

returned_title: Resonance of the Population to the Election Campaign and the Result of the Federal Parliament Election 1969
justification: A survey examining West German public reactions to the 1969 federal election campaign and its results. Topics include political interest, participation in election meetings, assessments of political parties and politicians, satisfaction with election outcomes, and preferences regarding government coalitions. It provides evidence about public perceptions of democratic institutions, political competition, and government formation. Relevant to political behavior and attitudes as well as government, political systems, and organizations during the 1960s.

returned_title: Cologne Election Study (Federal Republic, November 1961)
justification: Part of a three-wave election research project associated with the 1961 West German federal election. This wave was conducted after the formation of the new government, making it particularly useful for examining political attitudes in the context of electoral competition and government formation. The study provides historical survey evidence relevant to political behavior, democratic institutions, and the political system of the Federal Republic of Germany during the early 1960s.

returned_title: German Federal Election Studies, 1949–2005
justification: A collection of historical German election survey datasets maintained by GESIS, including studies associated with the 1961, 1965, and 1969 federal elections. The collection includes cross-sectional surveys, panel studies, and cumulative datasets examining political preferences, electoral behavior, and attitudes toward political parties and government. The 1960s studies are especially relevant for investigating changes in political participation, democratic attitudes, and political institutions across the decade. Individual studies can be located through the linked GESIS data catalog.

returned_title: German State Election Studies, 1962–2004
justification: A GESIS collection of representative surveys conducted in connection with elections in German federal states, beginning in 1962. The collection includes an integrated dataset covering 1962–2004, allowing researchers to investigate regional electoral behavior and political attitudes over time. The observations from the 1960s are particularly relevant for studying political participation, regional government, political parties, and the relationship between state-level and federal politics in West Germany. Researchers can select the relevant years to focus specifically on the 1960s.

returned_title: Reproductive Behavior of Women and Couples: Socioeconomic and Psychosocial Determinants, 1990 Population Survey
justification: Highly relevant to reproductive health in the former German Democratic Republic (GDR). This GESIS dataset examines reproductive behavior, family planning, and socioeconomic and psychosocial determinants among women aged 15–45 residing in East Berlin. Data were collected between September 1990 and October 1991, making it particularly valuable for studying reproductive health during German reunification.

returned_title: Courses of Life and Historical Change in East Germany (Life History Study LV-DDR)
justification: A highly relevant retrospective dataset examining family life, marriage, partnerships, childbirth, and household formation among individuals who lived in the former GDR. The study includes marital histories, information about spouses and children, family relationships, and comparisons between living conditions in East and West Germany. Data collected in the early 1990s provide insights into family structures established during the GDR period and their transformation following reunification.

returned_title: East German Life Courses After Unification (Life History Study LV-Ost 71)
justification: This GESIS dataset focuses on individuals born in 1971 who lived in East Germany in October 1990. Collected between May 1996 and June 1997, it includes detailed information about family backgrounds, partnerships, household arrangements, education, and employment. It is particularly useful for investigating how reunification affected marriage, family formation, and the transition to adulthood among people raised in the GDR.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel Study (SOEP-Core), Data 1984–2010
justification: A major longitudinal household survey that expanded into the former GDR in June 1990. It contains information on health status, household composition, marriage, family relationships, socioeconomic conditions, and life satisfaction. The 1990s waves are especially valuable for comparing the health and family circumstances of former East German residents before and after reunification. The dataset supports research on health inequalities, family transitions, and the social determinants of medical conditions.

returned_title: Saxony Longitudinal Study (Sächsische Längsschnittstudie)
justification: A longitudinal study that began in 1987 among young people in the GDR and continued through the 1990s and beyond. It documents changes in social attitudes, personal circumstances, and psychological well-being during German reunification. The study is relevant to research on mental health, health complaints, family planning, partnerships, and the long-term consequences of political and social transformation. The landing page provides access to information about datasets archived by GESIS.

returned_title: GESIS Microcensus Trendfile 1962–2016
justification: A harmonized collection of German Microcensus data that includes survey years 1991, 1993, and 1995–1999. It contains demographic and socioeconomic variables relating to household composition, marital status, family arrangements, and living conditions. The underlying post-reunification Microcensus files can support analysis of family and marriage patterns in the former East German states during the 1990s. Researchers should note that the harmonized trendfile primarily emphasizes West German historical comparisons, so geographic coverage must be checked for individual years.

returned_title: German Microcensus Scientific Use Files, 1991–1999
justification: The German Microcensus Scientific Use Files provide representative population data for the years immediately following reunification. The 1990s files can be used to examine marriage, divorce, household composition, parenthood, and family structures in the states of the former GDR. Selected survey years also contain health-related information, although medical variables and their availability differ by year. The linked GESIS page identifies the relevant annual files and provides information about their integration into longitudinal analyses.

returned_title: WHO MONICA Project: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Surveys in East Germany, 1982–1994
justification: Relevant to specific diseases, disorders, and medical conditions in the former GDR. The WHO MONICA project conducted population-based cardiovascular health surveys in East Germany during 1982–1984, 1987–1989, and 1991–1994. Data include blood pressure measurements, hypertension prevalence, body measurements, blood samples, and cardiovascular risk factors. The study enables comparisons between health conditions before and after reunification. The DOI identifies a research publication describing the underlying survey datasets rather than a direct data-download page.

returned_title: Reproductive Behavior of Women and Couples: GESIS Dataset Metadata
justification: The GESIS dataset metadata record provides additional documentation for the 1990–1991 reproductive health survey of women living in East Berlin. It identifies the study population, temporal coverage, research institutions, and access conditions. The record also references a supplementary survey of women undergoing abortions in an East Berlin clinic, archived as GESIS study ZA6386. This makes it a useful starting point for locating more specialized reproductive health data related to abortion and pregnancy during the final months of the GDR and the immediate post-reunification period.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Surveys 2010–2018
justification: One of the most comprehensive datasets for studying political attitudes, social stratification, inequality, minorities, and cultural identity in Germany during the 2010s. The biennial surveys conducted in 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, and 2018 contain information on political preferences, social class, education, income, migration backgrounds, national identity, attitudes toward immigrants, and perceptions of social inequality. Particularly useful for examining changes in German society throughout the decade.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUScompact) – Cumulation 1980–2023
justification: A harmonized longitudinal collection of German population surveys that includes observations from the entire 2010s. Covers political attitudes, social mobility, class identification, socioeconomic inequality, immigration, social integration, and cultural values. The cumulative structure facilitates comparisons between survey years and enables researchers to investigate long-term developments in political behavior, social exclusion, and national identity.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Federal Elections 2013 and 2017
justification: A major source of German electoral behavior and political attitudes during the 2010s. Includes surveys surrounding the 2013 and 2017 federal elections, covering voting intentions, party identification, political participation, ideological orientations, immigration attitudes, and demographic characteristics. Particularly valuable for studying how social class, education, economic inequality, and attitudes toward minorities influenced political preferences and electoral behavior.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Rolling Cross-Section 2013 and 2017
justification: Provides detailed survey data collected during German federal election campaigns in 2013 and 2017. Captures changes in voter preferences, political engagement, party evaluations, and attitudes toward major political issues. Particularly relevant for analyzing the relationship between political behavior, socioeconomic groupings, immigration debates, and changing national identity during election campaigns.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Long-Term Panel 2009–2017
justification: Longitudinal panel data following German voters across multiple federal elections, including the 2009–2013 and 2013–2017 election periods. Supports analysis of individual-level changes in political attitudes, voting behavior, and party identification. Useful for investigating how socioeconomic status, generational differences, cultural attitudes, and political developments shaped electoral behavior throughout the 2010s.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core) – Longitudinal Household Survey
justification: A major longitudinal household dataset covering Germany throughout the 2010s. Contains detailed information on income, wealth-related indicators, employment, education, household composition, migration backgrounds, subjective well-being, social participation, and attitudes. Particularly suitable for investigating economic inequality, social stratification, social mobility, immigrant integration, and differences between demographic groups. Annual observations enable detailed analysis of changes in social exclusion and socioeconomic disparities.

returned_title: GESIS Panel – German Population Panel Study, 2013–2019
justification: A representative longitudinal survey of Germany's adult German-speaking population, with data collection beginning in 2013. Includes measures of political participation, social attitudes, values, subjective well-being, and demographic characteristics. Particularly useful for investigating changes in political attitudes and social participation during the second half of the 2010s, including relationships between socioeconomic position and political engagement.

returned_title: GESIS Panel – Social and Political Participation, 2014–2019
justification: A longitudinal survey module measuring social and political participation among people living in Germany. Data collected throughout 2014–2019 can support research on political engagement, civic participation, and differences between social groups. Particularly relevant for examining how participation varies according to demographic characteristics and socioeconomic circumstances, helping identify inequalities in civic and political involvement.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) – Scientific Use Files, 2010s
justification: A large-scale longitudinal study examining educational pathways and social inequalities in Germany. Multiple starting cohorts were surveyed during the 2010s, providing information on educational achievement, family background, migration background, socioeconomic circumstances, and transitions into employment. Particularly useful for investigating social stratification, inequalities affecting minority groups, intergenerational mobility, and mechanisms of social exclusion within the German education system.

returned_title: IAB-BAMF-SOEP Survey of Refugees in Germany – Beginning in 2016
justification: A longitudinal survey focusing on refugees who arrived in Germany, particularly during the migration movements of the mid-2010s. Provides information on education, employment, integration, language acquisition, living conditions, and social participation. Particularly relevant for studying minority experiences, socioeconomic inequality, migration-related disadvantage, integration barriers, and social exclusion. The survey allows researchers to investigate changes in refugees' circumstances during the second half of the decade.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Social Inequality V, 2019
justification: An international comparative survey conducted in 2019 that includes Germany. Focuses specifically on perceptions of social inequality, social mobility, economic fairness, income differences, and attitudes toward redistribution. Particularly useful for analyzing how different socioeconomic groups in Germany perceived inequality at the end of the 2010s. The internationally harmonized structure also enables comparisons between Germany and other countries.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – National Identity Module
justification: The ISSP National Identity survey series includes a 2013 wave suitable for studying German national identity during the 2010s. Relevant measures include national pride, national belonging, citizenship, attitudes toward immigration, and perceptions of cultural differences. Particularly useful for examining relationships between national identity, minority attitudes, immigration, social boundaries, and political orientations in Germany.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Family and Changing Gender Roles IV, 2012
justification: An internationally comparative survey including Germany in 2012, focused on gender roles, family structures, employment, and attitudes toward the division of household and caregiving responsibilities. Useful for investigating gender inequality, cultural norms, social stratification, and differences in attitudes across demographic groups. Provides a valuable perspective on equality and changing social expectations in Germany during the early 2010s.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Work Orientations IV, 2015
justification: A comparative survey that includes Germany and focuses on employment attitudes, job characteristics, work preferences, and experiences in the labor market. Relevant for studying occupational stratification, differences between socioeconomic groups, employment-related inequality, and attitudes toward work. The 2015 data provide a mid-decade perspective on the relationship between labor market position and broader social attitudes.

returned_title: European Values Study (EVS) – Integrated Dataset 2017
justification: A cross-national survey including Germany that examines fundamental social, political, religious, and cultural values. The 2017 wave is particularly relevant for studying national identity, political trust, democratic values, immigration attitudes, tolerance of minorities, gender equality, and perceptions of social differences. Useful for understanding German cultural and political attitudes toward the end of the 2010s and comparing them with those of other European societies.

returned_title: European Values Study (EVS) – Trend File 1981–2017
justification: A harmonized dataset combining multiple waves of the European Values Study, including German observations from 2017. Provides measures of political values, trust, religion, national belonging, tolerance, family attitudes, and social norms. Particularly useful for placing German attitudes during the 2010s in a longer historical context and examining whether views about minorities, equality, and cultural identity changed across generations.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS) – German Survey Data, Rounds 5–9 (2010–2018)
justification: A major European comparative survey containing German data from multiple rounds throughout the 2010s. Covers political trust, electoral participation, democratic attitudes, immigration, discrimination, national and European identity, subjective well-being, social exclusion, and socioeconomic characteristics. Particularly valuable for comparing political and cultural attitudes across social classes, age groups, educational backgrounds, and migration-related groups. Its repeated cross-sectional design enables analysis of trends across the decade.

returned_title: German Microcensus (Mikrozensus) – Population and Social Structure Data, 2010–2019
justification: Germany's official annual household survey provides extensive information on demographic and socioeconomic characteristics during the 2010s. Particularly relevant variables include education, employment, occupation, household structure, migration background, and living conditions. Suitable for analyzing social stratification, socioeconomic inequalities, demographic differences, and structural disadvantages affecting immigrant populations and other social groups. Unlike attitude surveys, its principal strength is detailed population and social structure data.

returned_title: GESIS Research Data Centre Elections – Politbarometer and DeutschlandTREND Surveys
justification: An archive providing access to recurring German political opinion surveys, including Politbarometer and DeutschlandTREND observations from the 2010s. These surveys offer information on party preferences, political evaluations, government satisfaction, and attitudes toward important political issues. Particularly useful for analyzing political behavior and shifts in public opinion during major developments in Germany, including immigration debates and the emergence of new political divisions.

returned_title: GESIS German Survey Data Collection – ALLBUS, GLES, and Additional German Studies
justification: An official entry point to multiple German social science datasets with observations from the 2010s. Includes major surveys covering electoral behavior, political attitudes, inequality, demographic characteristics, social participation, and cultural values. Particularly useful for identifying additional studies on minorities, national identity, migration, and social exclusion and for locating associated questionnaires and documentation.

returned_title: Health 1990 (Gesundheit 1990)
justification: Highly relevant dataset covering health and health-related behavior in the German Democratic Republic (GDR) in 1990. Conducted by the Department of Medical Sociology at the Institute for Social Hygiene and Health Care Organization in Berlin, the study examines chronic diseases, health behaviors, nutrition, physical activity, alcohol consumption, smoking, and medical treatment. The survey covers individuals aged 14 and older, with data collection beginning in June 1990. It directly addresses all four requested categories: diet and nutrition, general health and well-being, medication and treatment, and specific diseases and medical conditions. Academic access is available, although publication of results requires additional permission.

returned_title: Outpatient Morbidity and Utilization of Outpatient Services, Görlitz I, 1986 – Population Survey
justification: A GDR health survey conducted in October 1986 among residents aged 18 and older in the Görlitz district. It investigates outpatient morbidity, medical consultations, healthcare utilization, and the relationship between residents and healthcare providers. Particularly relevant to medication and treatment, general health, and specific diseases and medical conditions during the 1980s. The dataset is archived by GESIS and requires written authorization from the data depositor for academic access.

returned_title: Eating Habits and Nutritional Status in Quedlinburg, 1985–1989: Third Substudy – Eating Habits of Pregnant Women
justification: A specialized nutrition dataset collected in the GDR between 1985 and 1987 as part of a larger investigation conducted between 1985 and 1989. Developed by the Central Institute for Nutrition of the GDR Academy of Sciences and Quedlinburg District Hospital, it examines the dietary habits of pregnant women. It contains weekly aggregated information about individual daily meals, making it particularly valuable for studying food consumption, maternal nutrition, reproductive health, and nutritional conditions in East Germany during the late 1980s.

returned_title: Eating Habits and Nutritional Status in Quedlinburg, 1985–1989: Second Substudy – Sociological Survey of Non-Pregnant Women
justification: A nutrition-related dataset from the GDR covering 1987–1988. It forms part of a ten-part investigation into the eating habits and nutritional status of pregnant women, nursing mothers, and infants. This substudy focuses on non-pregnant women aged 18–35 attending gynecological consultations at Quedlinburg District Hospital. It provides useful comparative information about women's nutritional circumstances and social conditions during the late 1980s. Particularly relevant to diet and nutrition, women's health, and general well-being.

returned_title: AIDS in the Consciousness of the Population of the GDR, 1989–1990
justification: A GDR population survey conducted in 1990 examining public awareness and perceptions of AIDS. Developed by the Institute for Sociology and Social Policy at the GDR Academy of Sciences and the Central Institute for Hygiene, Microbiology and Epidemiology, it focuses on an important infectious disease during the final years of East Germany. The survey covers the adult residential population, with data collection between July and October 1990. It is especially relevant to specific diseases and medical conditions, health awareness, public health education, and attitudes toward infectious diseases. The dataset is available for academic research and teaching.

returned_title: Life in the GDR 1990 (Leben in der DDR 1990)
justification: A January 1990 survey investigating social conditions and quality of life in the GDR during the beginning of political and economic transformation. Conducted by the Institute for Sociology and Social Policy at the GDR Academy of Sciences, it includes questions concerning health, healthy lifestyles, social security, living conditions, environmental protection, and life satisfaction. The study covers the districts of Potsdam, Leipzig, and Schwerin. It is particularly useful for understanding general health and well-being and the social determinants of health immediately before German reunification.

returned_title: HISTAT Online Data Compilation: Basic Data on the Development of Health Conditions in Germany, 1816–2010
justification: A historical statistical dataset compiled by Jürgen Sensch and archived by GESIS. It includes official statistical information from the former GDR alongside historical data from other German territories. The dataset covers mortality, life expectancy, age-specific death rates, and the historical development of public health. Its coverage includes the 1980s and 1990s, allowing researchers to examine health conditions in East Germany before and after reunification. Particularly relevant to general health and well-being and population-level patterns of disease and mortality.

returned_title: Statistical Overviews of Social Policy in Germany Since 1945: Soviet Occupation Zone and GDR
justification: A historical statistical collection compiled by André Steiner, covering social policy in the Soviet Occupation Zone and the GDR. The underlying statistical series extend from 1939 to 1996, with GDR-specific coverage ending in 1989. Sources include official GDR health statistics published in Das Gesundheitswesen der DDR between 1965 and 1988. The dataset provides historical quantitative evidence relevant to healthcare provision, social protection, and health-related public services. It is useful for examining the institutional and statistical context of general health, medical treatment, and healthcare policy during the 1980s.

returned_title: GDR Microdata – Official Statistics on Living Conditions, Income and Consumption
justification: A GESIS collection of microdata from official GDR statistics, including representative surveys of household income, consumption, and social living conditions toward the end of the 1980s. These datasets are relevant for investigating household consumption patterns, material living standards, and socioeconomic determinants of nutrition and health. They may help researchers examine the relationship between household resources, consumption, and well-being in late socialist East Germany. This is a collection-level landing page rather than an individual dataset, and the availability of specific food-consumption variables should be checked in the documentation.

returned_title: European System of Social Indicators: Health, 1980–2013
justification: A longitudinal statistical dataset covering health-related social indicators from 1980 to 2013 across more than 30 countries. It contains time-series information on individual well-being, quality of life, and broader societal conditions. Its historical coverage makes it potentially useful for comparing health developments in Germany during the 1980s and 1990s with developments in other European countries. However, the availability of separate GDR observations before reunification must be verified before using it for East German historical analysis.

returned_title: System of Social Indicators for the Federal Republic of Germany: Health
justification: A GESIS statistical dataset containing historical health indicators covering 1950–2013. It includes measures of life expectancy, causes of death, illness, disability, sick leave, outpatient medical treatment, hospital utilization, and regular medication use. The dataset is relevant to general health and well-being, medication and treatment, and specific diseases. Its coverage extends across the 1980s and 1990s, making it potentially useful for investigating health changes around German reunification. Researchers should verify which historical observations distinguish East Germany from West Germany, as pre-1990 data may primarily describe the former Federal Republic.

returned_title: Personal, Property and Social Insurance in the Former GDR, 1950–1989
justification: A historical statistical dataset covering insurance systems in the German Democratic Republic from 1950 to 1989. Compiled by Peter Borscheid and Anette Drees, it draws on historical insurance statistics and GDR statistical yearbooks. Although not primarily a medical or nutritional survey, it provides useful contextual information about social insurance arrangements and social protection during the 1980s. It may support research into the institutional conditions affecting healthcare access and general well-being in the GDR.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Federal Elections 2021 and 2025
justification: The German Longitudinal Election Study provides extensive survey datasets on political behaviour, voting decisions, party identification, political trust, electoral participation, and attitudes toward democracy in Germany. Its 2021 and 2025 election studies are particularly relevant for investigating political behaviour and attitudes during the 2020s. The collection includes cross-sectional surveys, panel studies, candidate studies, and election campaign tracking data.

returned_title: GLES Tracking 2009–2026 – Cumulative Dataset
justification: This longitudinal survey dataset tracks changes in German political attitudes, party preferences, government approval, political participation, and perceptions of political institutions. Its repeated measurements during the 2020s make it particularly useful for analysing changing political opinions, electoral volatility, and responses to major political developments.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – 2021, 2023 and 2025
justification: ALLBUS is a representative population survey examining social and political attitudes in Germany. Its datasets from the 2020s include information relevant to political trust, democratic values, social inequalities, immigration attitudes, political participation, and perceptions of government. The surveys facilitate comparisons across population groups and over time.

returned_title: German Federal Election 2025 – Official Electoral Results Open Data
justification: The Federal Returning Officer provides official machine-readable election results for Germany's 2025 Bundestag election. The datasets include votes for political parties and candidates, electoral constituencies, and geographic distributions of election results. Comparative data from the 2021 election are also provided. These data are essential for analysing electoral behaviour, party competition, political representation, and changes in Germany's party system.

returned_title: German Federal Election 2025 – Final Results by Constituency
justification: This official dataset provides final results of the 2025 German federal election at national, state, and constituency levels. It supports quantitative research on political party performance, voter turnout, regional political differences, and electoral representation. Historical election results also allow comparisons with the 2021 federal election.

returned_title: German Bundestag – Parliamentary Open Data
justification: The German Bundestag publishes machine-readable parliamentary records, legislative documents, member biographies, and recorded parliamentary votes. Data covering the 2020s enable research on parliamentary institutions, legislative behaviour, political parties, government accountability, parliamentary debates, and relationships between government and opposition.

returned_title: German Bundestag and Bundesrat – Parliamentary Documentation and Information System (DIP)
justification: The DIP database documents parliamentary proceedings, legislative initiatives, government proposals, parliamentary questions, and debates in Germany's federal political institutions. Records from the 2020s are particularly useful for studying government decision-making, legislative processes, institutional relationships, and the policy priorities of political parties.

returned_title: Manifesto Project Dataset – German Political Party Programmes
justification: The Manifesto Project provides systematically coded political party election programmes, including manifestos from German federal elections during the 2020s. Its variables capture party positions on democracy, governance, economic policy, immigration, European integration, foreign affairs, and international cooperation. The dataset is suitable for analysing political ideology, party competition, and changes in Germany's political system.

returned_title: Manifesto Project Dataset 2025a – Party Preferences
justification: This versioned dataset provides quantitative indicators derived from the election programmes of political parties across multiple countries, including Germany. It supports comparative research on German political parties' ideological positions, government policy priorities, international relations, European integration, and political representation during the 2020s.

returned_title: German Policy Agendas Project – Government, Parliament and Public Policy
justification: The German Policy Agendas Project provides datasets covering government speeches, parliamentary questions, legislative proposals, laws, and public perceptions of important political problems. Its coverage extends to 2021, making it useful for examining government priorities, parliamentary behaviour, political institutions, and policy agendas at the beginning of the 2020s.

returned_title: Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) – Germany Country-Year Data
justification: V-Dem provides annual indicators measuring democratic institutions, electoral systems, political participation, civil liberties, executive accountability, political equality, and institutional constraints on government power. Germany's observations during the 2020s can be used to assess democratic governance and political institutions and compare Germany with other European democracies.

returned_title: V-Dem – Democracy Dataset
justification: This international dataset offers detailed indicators of democratic governance and political systems, including electoral democracy, liberal democracy, deliberative democracy, and participatory democracy. Its Germany-specific country-year observations support research on the development of political institutions, democratic accountability, political participation, and governance throughout the 2020s.

returned_title: GLES European Parliament Election Candidate Study 2024
justification: The German Longitudinal Election Study includes a candidate study associated with the 2024 European Parliament election. It provides evidence relevant to political representation, candidate characteristics, political recruitment, European parliamentary politics, and the relationship between German political parties and European Union institutions.

returned_title: GLES Nomination Study 2021 and 2025
justification: These studies examine political candidate nomination processes surrounding Germany's 2021 and 2025 federal elections. They are relevant to research on party organisations, candidate selection, political recruitment, internal party structures, and political representation within the German parliamentary system.

returned_title: GLES – Coding of the Most Important Political Problem, 2018–2023
justification: This dataset systematically classifies survey responses about the most important political problems facing Germany. Its observations from 2020 through 2023 provide insight into public political priorities and concerns during the COVID-19 pandemic, changes in government, and major international political developments. It is particularly relevant for studying political attitudes and issue salience.

returned_title: United Nations General Assembly Voting Data – 1946 to September 2026
justification: This official United Nations dataset records how member states voted on General Assembly resolutions, including Germany's voting behaviour throughout the 2020s. It supports research on German foreign policy, international political cooperation, diplomatic alignment, multilateral institutions, and Germany's positions on international security and human rights.

returned_title: United Nations General Assembly Resolutions – Voting Data and Issue Categories
justification: This dataset combines United Nations General Assembly voting records with thematic classifications of resolutions. It covers the period from 1995 through January 2025 and includes Germany. Researchers can investigate Germany's voting behaviour on international security, human rights, economic cooperation, and other global political issues while comparing its positions with those of other countries.

returned_title: United Nations Voting Incidence and Coincidence – 2025 Dataset
justification: This Harvard Dataverse dataset provides voting records and measures of agreement between countries in the United Nations General Assembly, Security Council, and Human Rights Council through 2025. Germany-specific observations can be used to examine international political alignment, diplomatic relationships, multilateral cooperation, and changes in German foreign policy during the 2020s.

returned_title: ManifestoVault – Annotated Election Manifestos from Germany, Ireland and the United Kingdom, 1970–2025
justification: ManifestoVault provides annotated election manifesto texts from political parties in Germany, Ireland, and the United Kingdom, including documents from the 2020s. The sentence-level annotations support computational analysis of political communication, party ideology, policy preferences, European integration, international relations, and changes in political discourse.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2023
justification: A longitudinal household and individual survey covering Germany, including every year from 2000 to 2009. Particularly relevant because it combines employment, occupational characteristics, income, job satisfaction, psychological well-being, life satisfaction, health, and personality-related measures. Suitable for investigating relationships between employment conditions, organizational experiences, and psychological outcomes during the 2000s. The linked DOI identifies the teaching edition.

returned_title: IAB Establishment Panel (IAB-Betriebspanel), 1993–2019
justification: A representative annual survey of German establishments covering the entire 2000–2009 period. Provides establishment-level information on employment, workforce composition, recruitment, organizational practices, personnel management, vocational training, working arrangements, and business development. Especially useful for research on industrial management, business organization, human resource management, and employment practices in German firms.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2006: Working Conditions and Occupational Qualifications
justification: A nationally representative survey of approximately 20,000 employed individuals in Germany conducted in 2005–2006. Contains detailed information on employment, occupational qualifications, workplace organization, job requirements, working conditions, occupational stressors, and health complaints. Particularly valuable for interdisciplinary research connecting employment, organizational psychology, workplace stress, and employee well-being.

returned_title: Linked Employer-Employee Data of the IAB (LIAB), Longitudinal Model 1975–2017
justification: A German longitudinal dataset linking establishment survey information with employee administrative employment records. Includes the complete 2000–2009 period. Enables research on organizational characteristics, employment relationships, workforce structure, wages, job mobility, and employer-level personnel practices. Particularly useful for studying how business organization and management relate to employee labor-market outcomes. Access is restricted through the IAB Research Data Centre.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), Cumulation 1980–2014
justification: A cumulative dataset containing nationally representative German social surveys, including waves conducted in 2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, and 2008. Covers employment status, occupational characteristics, social attitudes, subjective perceptions, values, and socioeconomic circumstances. Relevant for social psychology, occupational attitudes, employment research, and relationships between work and broader social attitudes in Germany during the 2000s.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2006: Working Conditions and Health
justification: The German Federal Institute for Occupational Safety and Health provides an official research resource for the 2006 employment survey, emphasizing occupational demands, workplace exposures, work-related strain, and health outcomes. Particularly relevant to occupational psychology, psychological stress at work, employee health, and the relationship between organizational working conditions and well-being. This is an alternative official landing page for the BIBB/BAuA 2006 survey.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Surveys, 1979–2006
justification: A collection of representative German employment surveys examining occupational qualifications, workplace technologies, job characteristics, and changing working conditions. The 1998–1999 and 2005–2006 waves are particularly useful for investigating changes around and during the 2000s. Relevant to organizational change, industrial management, technological transformation, occupational demands, and employee experiences.

returned_title: BIBB Cost-Benefit Surveys of Apprenticeship Training, 2000 and 2007
justification: Firm-level surveys conducted by Germany's Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training. The 2000 and 2007 waves provide evidence about the costs and benefits of workplace apprenticeship training. Particularly relevant to business management, personnel development, organizational investment in human capital, workforce training, and industrial employment practices. The linked BIBB data catalogue provides information about accessing these surveys.

returned_title: BIBB Transition Survey 2006
justification: A representative German survey examining young people's educational and occupational transitions. The 2006 survey is relevant to employment, career development, occupational decision-making, and the transition from education into work. It can support research connecting labor-market opportunities with behavioral and psychological aspects of career choice, although the availability of specific psychological measures should be checked in the documentation.

returned_title: BIBB School Graduate Surveys, 2004–2008
justification: A collection of representative surveys of German school graduates, including the years 2004, 2005, 2006, and 2008. Examines occupational preferences, employment expectations, educational pathways, and career decisions. Relevant to vocational psychology, employment expectations, occupational aspirations, workforce entry, and human resource development. The BIBB research data catalogue provides access information.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), Individual Surveys 2000–2008
justification: The official GESIS repository provides access to individual ALLBUS survey waves for 2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, and 2008. These surveys contain information on social attitudes, employment, occupational characteristics, socioeconomic background, and subjective evaluations. Useful for examining psychological and social attitudes in relation to employment and occupational position. Individual waves can be analyzed separately or combined to investigate changes throughout the decade.

returned_title: IAB Establishment Panel, 1993–2022
justification: A longitudinal establishment-level dataset covering Germany from 1993 through 2022, including all years from 2000 to 2009. Provides information on business structures, employment demand, personnel policies, workforce organization, training, and establishment characteristics. Well suited to analyzing organizational management decisions and their consequences for employment. This is a more recent version of the IAB Establishment Panel listed above.

returned_title: Harmonized BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey Dataset, 2006–2018
justification: A harmonized dataset combining the 2006, 2012, and 2018 German employment surveys. Although only the 2006 wave falls within the requested decade, the harmonized structure enables comparisons between working conditions in the 2000s and subsequent periods. Covers occupational tasks, employment characteristics, work demands, and related workplace experiences. Particularly useful for research on organizational changes and occupational health over time.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2006, GESIS Scientific Use File
justification: A scientific-use version of the German 2006 employment survey distributed through GESIS. Provides individual-level information on qualifications, occupational activities, employment conditions, workplace requirements, and work-related experiences. Suitable for studying work organization, occupational stress, employee satisfaction, and relationships between work characteristics and psychological or health outcomes. This is another access route to the BIBB/BAuA 2006 survey.

returned_title: BAuA Working Time Survey 2015 (BAuA-Arbeitszeitbefragung 2015)
justification: A nationally representative German working-time survey conducted by the Federal Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (BAuA). Covers working hours, flexible working arrangements, telecommuting, occupational demands, work-life balance, and employee well-being. Particularly useful for establishing a baseline for telecommuting and work intensification in Germany before the widespread adoption of remote work. Can support research on potential indicators of workaholism, such as excessive working hours and insufficient recovery.

returned_title: BAuA Working Time Survey 2017 (BAuA-Arbeitszeitbefragung 2017)
justification: A follow-up survey covering German employees' working conditions, telecommuting, working from home, mobile work, flexibility, autonomy, and occupational health. Includes information about working-time arrangements, recovery, psychological demands, and work-life balance. Highly relevant for examining relationships between digitalized working arrangements, telecommuting, excessive working hours, and employee well-being during the 2010s. Its longitudinal design supports comparisons with the 2015 and 2019 waves.

returned_title: BAuA Working Time Survey 2019 (BAuA-Arbeitszeitbefragung 2019)
justification: A German working-time dataset covering the final year of the 2010s. Contains information on telecommuting, flexible working arrangements, working-time variability, psychological and physical demands, and employee satisfaction. Particularly suitable for investigating how increasingly flexible and digitally enabled work arrangements relate to working intensity, overtime, and employee well-being. Together with the 2015 and 2017 waves, it enables analysis of pre-pandemic developments in German telecommuting.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2018 (Erwerbstätigenbefragung 2018)
justification: A representative survey of approximately 20,000 employed individuals in Germany, conducted in 2017–2018 by the Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training (BIBB) and BAuA. Covers occupational tasks, technological changes, working conditions, job demands, qualifications, occupational stress, and health. Especially relevant for studying workplace digitalization and its relationship with employee working conditions and potential performance-related outcomes. Variables concerning occupational demands and stress may also provide indirect indicators of workaholism-related conditions.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2012 (Erwerbstätigenbefragung 2012)
justification: A large-scale German employment survey documenting occupational characteristics, job requirements, working conditions, technological equipment, qualifications, and occupational health in 2012. Particularly valuable as an early-2010s benchmark for studying digitalization and changes in workplace demands. Comparison with the 2018 survey can help identify developments in technology-related work, occupational stress, and working conditions over the decade.

returned_title: Linked Personnel Panel 2016/2017 (LPP 1617)
justification: An integrated employer-employee dataset developed by Germany's Institute for Employment Research (IAB). Combines establishment-level information with employee survey responses, enabling research on personnel management, workplace organization, employee attitudes, job quality, and organizational practices. Particularly relevant for investigating relationships between digitalized work organization, employee motivation, working conditions, and job performance-related outcomes. The linked employer-employee structure is especially useful for multilevel analyses of organizational and individual factors.

returned_title: Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), Germany, 1984–2022
justification: One of Germany's major longitudinal household panel datasets, administered by the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin). Includes annual information about employment, working hours, income, occupational characteristics, job satisfaction, health, and individual well-being. Data from 2010–2019 can be selected for historical analysis. Particularly useful for investigating associations between working arrangements, extended working hours, job satisfaction, and employee well-being. Relevant waves and variables should be checked for direct measures of working from home and digitalization; workaholism and job performance may require proxy measures.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2018 – Campus File
justification: A reduced, research-oriented version of the 2018 German Employment Survey designed for teaching and introductory empirical analysis. Provides selected information on employment characteristics, occupational tasks, working conditions, and job demands. Useful for preliminary investigations of digitalization, work intensity, and occupational outcomes before requesting access to the more comprehensive Scientific Use File. Its reduced variable coverage may limit detailed analysis of telecommuting, workaholism, and job performance.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2012 – Campus File
justification: A reduced version of the 2012 German Employment Survey suitable for exploratory research and statistical training. Contains selected employment and occupational characteristics that can support comparisons of working conditions and occupational demands during the early 2010s. Particularly useful when combined conceptually with the 2018 Campus File to investigate changes in German working environments. Researchers requiring detailed technological, telecommuting, or performance-related measures should consult the full Scientific Use Files.

returned_title: BAuA Working Time Survey – Research Data Center and Longitudinal Dataset Collection
justification: The official research data portal for the BAuA Working Time Survey, providing access information and documentation for the 2015, 2017, and 2019 waves. Especially valuable for identifying comparable variables covering telecommuting, mobile work, working-time flexibility, overtime, psychological demands, and employee well-being. The documentation helps determine which variables can operationalize digitalization, telecommuting, and workaholism-related behavior across the decade. Direct measures of work addiction and objective job performance should not be assumed without checking the questionnaires.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Surveys 2012 and 2018 – Official Research Data Collection
justification: The official BIBB research data portal for German employment surveys, including the 2012 and 2018 datasets. Provides information about available Scientific Use Files, supplementary variables, access procedures, and research documentation. Especially useful for investigating changes in occupational technology, digitalization, employee qualifications, work demands, and working conditions throughout the 2010s. The two survey waves offer repeated cross-sectional evidence on changes in German employment rather than a longitudinal panel following the same employees.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2018 – Detailed Dataset Metadata
justification: The official metadata record for the 2018 German Employment Survey. Describes the dataset's coverage, research topics, documentation, and available supplementary data. Particularly useful for identifying variables relevant to digitalization, occupational stress, job demands, and working conditions before applying for data access. Researchers examining workaholism and job performance can use the metadata to assess whether suitable direct measures or theoretically defensible proxies are available.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Surveys 2006–2024 – Interactive Data Visualization
justification: An official interactive data resource providing selected indicators from German employment surveys, including the 2012 and 2018 waves. Covers working conditions, occupational demands, work-related resources, job satisfaction, and health complaints. Particularly useful for exploratory comparisons of work intensification and employee well-being during the 2010s. Selected results can be exported as tables, although this resource does not replace the underlying individual-level survey datasets.

returned_title: Leisure Time 1969 (Freizeit 1969) – German Democratic Republic
justification: Highly relevant historical survey dataset examining leisure activities, sports participation, tourism, cultural interests, and youth lifestyles in East Germany in 1969. Variables include preferred leisure activities, organized and informal sports participation, attendance at cultural events, weekend excursions, foreign holidays, vacation preferences, friendships, and membership in the Free German Youth (FDJ). Particularly valuable for studying the relationship between youth, recreation, sports, and tourism during the late 1960s. The dataset is associated with the GESIS Data Catalogue.

returned_title: Deutschland in Daten – Culture, Tourism and Sport: Historical Statistical Series
justification: Historical statistical dataset covering Germany from 1834 to 2018, including separate series for West Germany and East Germany during 1949–1989. Particularly relevant for examining tourism, cultural participation, leisure infrastructure, sports clubs, and sports association membership during the 1960s. Provides quantitative historical indicators suitable for comparing leisure and recreational developments between the Federal Republic of Germany and the German Democratic Republic.

returned_title: Deutschland in Daten – Culture, Tourism and Sport (Kultur, Tourismus und Sport)
justification: Historical statistical compilation containing long-term data series on tourism, cinema attendance, cultural activities, sports organizations, and sports club membership. Includes information on the expansion of tourism infrastructure during the 1950s and 1960s, domestic tourism in East Germany, and the growth of organized sport. Particularly useful for contextualizing youth leisure opportunities and the expansion of recreational activities in both German states during the 1960s.

returned_title: German Historical Time Series Dataset, 1834–2018 – Documentation and Statistical Tables
justification: Comprehensive historical statistical resource containing documented German time series, including observations from the 1960s. Covers social, demographic, economic, cultural, and recreational developments. Particularly valuable for locating historical statistics concerning tourism, sports organizations, educational participation, and demographic changes affecting young people. Includes source documentation and statistical tables that support longitudinal comparisons between East and West Germany.

returned_title: GESIS Microcensus Trendfile 1962–2016
justification: Harmonized microdata covering population and social change in West Germany beginning in 1962. Includes data from the annual microcensuses conducted between 1962 and 1969, enabling detailed analysis of young people by age, education, employment, household characteristics, and socioeconomic background. Although it does not primarily focus on sports or tourism, it provides valuable demographic and social context for studying youth leisure opportunities and changing living conditions during the 1960s.

returned_title: German Microcensus 1962–1969 – GESIS Historical Microdata Files
justification: Collection of historical microcensus datasets covering West Germany annually from 1962 through 1969. Contains individual-level demographic and socioeconomic information based on approximately 1% of the population. Particularly useful for investigating youth demographics, educational participation, employment patterns, and household circumstances during the 1960s. The files can support research on the social conditions influencing recreational participation, leisure opportunities, and tourism.

returned_title: Deutschland in Daten – Culture and Tourism Historical Statistics
justification: English-language presentation of historical German statistics on culture, leisure, tourism, and sport. Includes statistical tables and historical analysis covering developments during the 1960s, such as tourism infrastructure growth, overnight stays, cinema attendance, and the expansion of recreational activities. Particularly useful for comparing tourism development and leisure opportunities in East and West Germany during the postwar economic expansion.

returned_title: Deutschland in Daten – Historical Dataset Documentation
justification: Provides access to detailed documentation, historical statistical tables, source references, and methodological explanations accompanying the German historical time series dataset. Particularly useful for identifying specific observations from 1960–1969 relating to cultural participation, tourism, sports clubs, and demographic developments. Supports verification of historical figures and identification of differences between East German and West German statistical coverage.

returned_title: Landtagswahl im Saarland 2012 (State Election in Saarland 2012) — GESIS ZA5642
justification: Directly relevant dataset examining the 2012 Saarland state parliamentary election. Part of the GESIS collection of German state election studies, which primarily consists of representative electoral surveys. Useful for investigating voting intentions, party preferences, political attitudes, electoral behaviour, and factors influencing voting decisions in Saarland. Particularly valuable for studying political behaviour during the early 2010s.

returned_title: Landtagswahl im Saarland 2017 (State Election in Saarland 2017) — GESIS ZA6948
justification: Directly relevant dataset covering the 2017 Saarland state parliamentary election. Archived by GESIS as part of its German state election studies. Suitable for studying electoral preferences, political attitudes, party evaluations, and voting behaviour surrounding the 2017 election. Especially useful for comparing political behaviour and electoral developments between the 2012 and 2017 Saarland elections.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES): Pre- and Post-Election Cross-Section 2013 — GESIS ZA5702
justification: National election survey dataset covering political attitudes and electoral behaviour surrounding the 2013 German federal election. Includes information on voting decisions, political preferences, and attitudes toward political parties and candidates. Potentially useful for analysing Saarland respondents within the broader German electorate, subject to the availability of suitable regional identifiers and sufficient Saarland observations.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES): Pre- and Post-Election Cross-Section 2017 — GESIS ZA6802
justification: Survey dataset examining political attitudes and voting behaviour before and after the 2017 German federal election. Provides information on electoral choices, political orientations, party preferences, and candidate evaluations. Relevant for investigating political behaviour among Saarland residents during the same year as the 2017 Saarland state election. Regional analysis depends on access to appropriate geographic identifiers.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES): Rolling Cross-Section 2013 — GESIS ZA5703
justification: Election campaign survey conducted around the 2013 German federal election. Provides data for studying changes in voting intentions, political attitudes, and party preferences during an election campaign. Potentially useful for examining Saarland voters in the context of national political developments, provided respondents can be geographically identified.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES): Rolling Cross-Section 2017 — GESIS ZA6803
justification: Survey covering the 2017 German federal election campaign, with information about political preferences, electoral intentions, and political attitudes. Particularly relevant for studying political behaviour in Saarland during 2017 and comparing regional political trends with national electoral dynamics. Saarland-specific analysis requires suitable geographic variables and adequate sample sizes.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES): Rolling Cross-Section Cumulation 2009–2017 — GESIS ZA6834
justification: Cumulative election survey dataset covering multiple German federal election campaigns between 2009 and 2017. Useful for longitudinal comparisons of political attitudes, electoral preferences, and voting intentions throughout much of the 2010s. Potentially valuable for examining changes among Saarland respondents across election cycles, subject to regional data availability.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES): Sensitive Regional Data — GESIS ZA6828
justification: Special GLES data release containing sensitive regional information for election studies conducted between 2013 and 2021. Particularly relevant for researchers seeking to identify respondents geographically and examine political attitudes and electoral behaviour in Saarland. Regional data access may be restricted, and availability of geographic identifiers does not guarantee representative Saarland-specific estimates.

returned_title: Politbarometer: German Political Opinion Surveys, 2010–2019 — GESIS
justification: Collection of approximately monthly representative surveys examining political attitudes among German voters. Covers party preferences, voting intentions, evaluations of politicians, political issues, and public opinion. Annual cumulative datasets and time-series data make the collection useful for studying political changes throughout the 2010s. Relevant to Saarland when regional identifiers or Saarland-specific survey observations are available.

returned_title: German State Election Studies (Landtagswahlen) — GESIS Research Data Collection
justification: Official GESIS dataset catalogue containing survey studies of elections to German state parliaments. Explicitly lists the Saarland elections of 2012 (ZA5642) and 2017 (ZA6948), with links to their dataset records. Particularly useful for discovering and comparing Saarland-specific electoral surveys, researching political behaviour and attitudes, and accessing accompanying study documentation.

returned_title: The Development of the Educational System in Germany: Comprehensive Schools 1960–2000
justification: GESIS historical education dataset covering Germany from 1960 to 2000. Contains national-level statistical time series on primary and secondary education, vocational training, universities, and population characteristics. Particularly relevant to higher and further education, educational expansion, and social stratification during the 1960s. Data for 1960–1990 refer to West Germany.

returned_title: GESIS Microcensus-Trendfile 1962–2016
justification: Harmonized collection of German Microcensus data beginning in 1962, including observations from the 1960s. Provides information on educational attainment, vocational qualifications, further training, employment, household composition, and demographic characteristics. Particularly valuable for studying social stratification, occupational mobility, educational inequalities, and socioeconomic groupings in West Germany.

returned_title: Preconditions of the Formation of Public Opinion in the Federal Republic of Germany, 1964
justification: Collection of four nationally sampled surveys of the West German electorate conducted in 1964 by the Konrad Adenauer Foundation. Examines attitudes toward the federal government, political parties, politicians, and domestic and foreign political issues. Highly relevant to political behaviour and attitudes, government and political organisations, international politics, and public opinion formation. Also useful for investigating political communication and the social characteristics of voters.

returned_title: Public Opinion Surveys: West Germany, November 1968
justification: Survey of 666 adults in West Germany conducted in November 1968. Investigates political attitudes, assessments of the chancellor and president, opinions about political parties, economic expectations, and perceptions of community problems and government responses. Relevant to political behaviour, political institutions, government performance, and socioeconomic attitudes during the politically significant year of 1968.

returned_title: Public Opinion Surveys: West Germany, December 1968
justification: Public opinion survey of 712 adults in West Germany conducted in December 1968 by the Konrad Adenauer Foundation. Includes attitudes toward government leaders, political parties, inflation, economic circumstances, and local administrative responses. Useful for analysing political attitudes, government legitimacy, socioeconomic perceptions, and changes in public opinion between November and December 1968.

returned_title: Political and Economic Attitudes of the Berlin Population, February–March 1967
justification: GESIS dataset examining political and economic attitudes among Berlin residents in 1967. Covers political knowledge, political participation, party preferences, voting intentions, satisfaction with political leaders, membership in organisations, and media usage. Also investigates perceptions of Western powers' interests in Berlin, making it particularly relevant to international politics, Cold War relations, media, political behaviour, government, and social groupings.

returned_title: German Federal Election Studies, 1949–2005
justification: GESIS collection containing historical German federal election surveys, including the 1961, 1965, and 1969 federal elections. Provides a major source for investigating voting behaviour, party preferences, political attitudes, electoral competition, and political institutions in West Germany. The collection includes cross-sectional, panel, and cumulative election studies, enabling comparisons of political change throughout the 1960s. Individual study records and downloadable data can be located through the GESIS catalogue.

returned_title: German State Election Studies, 1962 onward
justification: GESIS election data collection including studies associated with German state elections beginning in 1962. Relevant to political behaviour, attitudes toward political parties, electoral participation, and regional political institutions during the 1960s. Particularly useful for investigating differences between German federal states and understanding the relationship between regional political systems and national politics.

returned_title: European Public Opinion and Foreign Policy: A Continuity Dataset, 1952–1970
justification: Historical comparative survey dataset covering public opinion on foreign and security policy in West Germany, France, Italy, and the United Kingdom during the 1950s and 1960s. Includes attitudes concerning international alliances, military strength, East–West relations, and foreign policy. Particularly relevant to international politics and organisations, Cold War political attitudes, and public perceptions of international security. The linked publication describes the dataset and its construction.

returned_title: GESIS Research Data Center Elections
justification: Official research data centre providing access to historical German federal and state election datasets, including federal elections from 1949 and state election studies from 1962. Particularly useful for locating individual datasets from the 1960s concerning political behaviour, political attitudes, government institutions, political parties, and electoral participation. This is a collection-level access point rather than a single dataset.

returned_title: GESIS Research Data Archive
justification: Official German social science data archive containing historical survey and statistical datasets relevant to Germany in the 1960s. Its holdings include election studies, political opinion surveys, historical education statistics, and demographic and socioeconomic research. Useful for identifying additional studies concerning higher education, media consumption, political institutions, international relations, social stratification, and group membership. This is a repository landing page rather than an individual dataset.

returned_title: ACLED – Armed Conflict Location & Event Data: Protest Events in Germany (2020–2026)
justification: A major event-level dataset documenting protests, demonstrations, riots, and political violence across Germany, including Berlin, from 2020 onward. Records include event dates, geographic locations, actors, protest types, and descriptions. Particularly useful for examining the 2024 farmers' protests, climate activism, environmental movements, and demonstrations concerning agricultural and food policy. Data can be filtered by Germany, Berlin, date, and event category.

returned_title: POLIZEI STRESSI – Berlin Demonstrations and Assemblies Dataset (2021–2026)
justification: An archive of official Berlin police registration data covering demonstrations and public assemblies since 2021. Includes dates, locations, demonstration topics, and geographic distributions. Particularly relevant for identifying agricultural protests, farmers' demonstrations, climate activism, and food-policy mobilization in Berlin. The dataset supports analysis of protest frequency, geographic concentration, and changes in mobilization over time.

returned_title: German Protest Registrations – Demonstrations in German Cities
justification: A research dataset compiling administrative records of registered demonstrations in German cities. It provides information about protest events and their characteristics, offering an alternative to media-based protest event datasets. Useful for comparing protest mobilization across German cities and investigating the geographic distribution of demonstrations related to agricultural policy, environmental regulation, and broader political movements.

returned_title: Berlin Open Data – Registered Public Assemblies (Versammlungen im Land Berlin)
justification: An official German government data catalog entry for registered public assemblies in Berlin. Relevant for studying the spatial and temporal distribution of demonstrations and identifying protests concerning agricultural subsidies, farming conditions, food systems, and environmental policy. Provides an official administrative source that can complement ACLED records.

returned_title: FragDenStaat – Berlin Demonstrations and Assemblies, 2023–2024
justification: A freedom-of-information request seeking detailed Berlin assembly records for 2023 and 2024, including dates, locations, and demonstration purposes where available. Particularly relevant to the major German farmers' protests in January 2024. This is a data-access request rather than a guaranteed downloadable dataset; the associated records and responses should be checked for availability.

returned_title: GESIS – Right-Wing Extremist Mobilization in Germany
justification: A research dataset on right-wing extremist demonstrations and political mobilization in Germany, with data collection extending into the 2020s. Useful for studying relationships between protest movements, political radicalization, and mobilization around government policy. It can provide contextual information when examining the political environment surrounding agricultural protests, although it does not specifically measure agricultural or nutrition policy.

returned_title: ProLoc – German Local Protest Dataset (2000–2020)
justification: A systematic protest-event dataset covering Bremen, Dresden, Leipzig, and Stuttgart through 2020. Includes protest forms, demands, organizers, and participating social groups. Useful for establishing historical baselines and comparing early-2020 protest activity with later agricultural and environmental movements. Geographic coverage does not include Berlin, and coverage of the 2020s is limited to 2020.

returned_title: Institute for Protest and Social Movement Studies – Harmonized Protest Survey Data
justification: A collection of 31 harmonized protest surveys from Germany and Poland, announced in 2026. The surveys provide participant-level information about motivations, political attitudes, and sociodemographic characteristics. Relevant for understanding who participates in German protest movements and why. Individual survey dates and protest topics should be checked before selecting data for agricultural or nutrition-policy research.

returned_title: European Commission – Common Agricultural Policy 2023–2027 Performance Monitoring and Evaluation Indicators
justification: An official European Commission data portal containing indicators measuring implementation and performance of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) during 2023–2027. Germany-specific data can be selected to examine agricultural subsidies, environmental objectives, rural development, planned interventions, and policy outcomes. Especially useful for connecting agricultural protest movements with changes in agricultural policy and public funding.
